title: Kélian Sommer
text:
Hi! I am a French Postdoctoral Researcher Associate at the Steward Observatory of the University of Arizona, in Tucson, United States.
I completed my PhD in astrophysics at the Laboratoire Univers et Particules de Montpellier (CNRS/IN2P3) in November 2024, during which I specialized in high-precision photometry and the characterization of instrumental and atmospheric transmissions, contributing to experiments such as StarDICE within the Dark Energy Science Collaboration of the Legacy Survey of Space and Time of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and the Zwicky Transient Facility.
Before my PhD, I graduated from a Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering at ESTACA Paris-Saclay in 2021.
My current research focuses primarily on the development, optimization, and testing of next-generation photon-counting UV optimized Skipper CCD detectors.

Jan 2025 –Present


Postdoctoral Research Fellow / Research Associate, University of Arizona, Steward Observatory, Tucson, Arizona, USA


Development, laboratory characterisation and performance optimisation of low-noise photon-counting Skipper CCD detectors for space-based UV astronomy.


Design and implementation of optical test setups for detector validation and performance assessment.


Noise modelling, sensitivity analysis and identification of limiting performance drivers.


Hands-on work with ultra-high vacuum equipment, sensitive electronics and optoelectronic hardware in clean-room environments.






Feb 2021 –Aug 2021


Research Engineer (Internship), Université de Montpellier, Laboratoire Univers et Particules de Montpellier (CNRS/IN2P3), Montpellier, France


Prototyping of an uncooled infrared thermal camera instrument for atmospheric characterisation.






Jun 2020 –Sep 2020


Instrumentation Engineer (Internship), Centre de Physique des Particules de Marseille (CNRS/IN2P3), Marseille, France


Development of a control & command infrastructure for a LISA prototype optical bench.
